subtitle: The Krobo millet festival and new year
answer: Ngmayem, “the eating of millet”, is the harvest festival of the Manya Krobo people at Odumase-Krobo in the Eastern Region and marks the start of the Krobo new year. It is held at the end of October: the 133rd edition runs from Sunday 25 October to Monday 2 November 2026, with a pilgrimage to Krobo Mountain and a grand durbar.

sections.title: What Ngmayem means
sections.html:
Ngmayem means “the eating of millet”, from the Dangme ngma, millet, and yemi, to eat. It celebrates the harvest and the Krobo farming tradition and marks the start of the Krobo new year.[[1,2]]

It was first instituted in 1893 as Hieyemi by the Konor Sir Emmanuel Mate-Kole; his successor renamed it Ngmayem in 1944.[[1]]

days.label: From 25 October
days.title: Opening events
days.html: Yokama, a celebration of ideal womanhood, and a mock durbar by basic school pupils.[[1]]

days.label: The week
days.title: To the mausoleum and the mountain
days.html: Akleme, a procession to the royal mausoleum, and Klowem Yami, a pilgrimage up Krobo Mountain, the old Krobo homeland, with hiking and music.[[1]]

days.label: Climax
days.title: The grand durbar
days.html: A grand durbar of chiefs, queen mothers, guests and citizens, alongside the Miss Ngmayem pageant, closing with a thanksgiving service on 2 November.[[1]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Odumase-Krobo is in the Eastern Region near Somanya, about two hours north-east of Accra.
Krobo Mountain: the pilgrimage involves a hike. Wear good shoes and carry water.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
Krobo beads: the area is famous for its glass beads. The Thursday bead market in Agomanya is nearby.
